intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Fiordland National Park, Te Anau Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Milford Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of the world's greatest walks through Fiordland National Park, passing stunning valleys, waterfalls, and alpine scenery over 4 days. Book huts in advance through DOC. The trail winds from Lake Te Anau to Milford Sound through pristine wilderness.

experiences.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungee Jump
experiences.description: Take the plunge at the world's first commercial bungee jumping site, a 43-metre jump above the stunning turquoise Kawarau River. Watch others jump from the viewing platform before taking your own leap. An iconic adrenaline experience that started it all in 1988.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Day Hike
experiences.description: Explore a section of the famous Routeburn Track, one of New Zealand's Great Walks, offering breathtaking alpine views, glacier-carved valleys, and diverse native birdlife. The track traverses the boundary of two national parks and rewards hikers with panoramic mountain vistas.

experiences.name: Hanmer Springs Bungy & Swing
experiences.description: Experience the Hanmer Springs Bungy, a 35-metre jump over a scenic river gorge, combined with the thrilling Ledge Swing for a double adrenaline hit. Set in the picturesque alpine village of Hanmer Springs, this is a more intimate and scenic bungee experience away from the Queenstown crowds.
experiences.location: Hanmer Springs Adventure Centre, Hanmer Springs

experiences.name: Abel Tasman Coast Track Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Abel Tasman National Park along golden sandy beaches, turquoise bays, and lush native forest. This accessible coastal walk offers a unique combination of beach and bush hiking, with opportunities to spot fur seals and native birds. Water taxis can be used to customize your route.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Fiordland National Park, Te Anau Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Day Hike

The track traverses the boundary of two national parks and rewards hikers with panoramic mountain vistas.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 - no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Christchurch or Queenstown airport at 13:00. Pick up a budget rental car (pre-booked) and drive toward Te Anau. If arriving in Queenstown (~4.5 hrs to Te Anau), stop at a roadside lookout along State Highway 6 through the Remarkables mountain range for scenic photos. Grab supplies at a supermarket in Queenstown (Countdown or Pak'nSave) to stock up on budget groceries for the week.
day_by_day.evening: Continue drive to Te Anau and check into Te Anau Boutique Stay in Fiordland National Park. Settle in, unpack, and take a short stroll along the Te Anau lakefront to stretch your legs after the flight. Watch the sunset over Lake Te Anau — free and stunning.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or airport cafe snack upon arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a meal deal sandwich or pie from a New World or BP service station en route (~NZD $8-10)
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta or rice dish using groceries purchased in Queenstown (~NZD $5-8 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is primarily a travel/arrival day. Prioritize rest after the long-haul flight. Pre-booking a budget rental car (e.g., Jucy or Omega Rentals) is essential for South Island travel. Stock up on groceries as Te Anau has limited and pricier supermarket options.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning walk along the Te Anau lakefront trail (free). Visit the Te Anau DOC Visitor Centre to get trail maps, weather updates, and advice on Fiordland hikes. Pick up any Great Walk passes or day hike permits needed for the week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Kepler Track trailhead (10 min from Te Anau township) and hike the Kepler Track Day Walk to Brod Bay (~2 hrs return, 5.5 km). Enjoy stunning lake views, beech forest, and birdlife including kea and fantails. This is a free, well-marked trail perfect for acclimatizing after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Te Anau township. Browse the small lakefront area. Cook a hearty self-catered dinner at the accommodation to save money.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered oats or toast with peanut butter at accommodation (~NZD $2-3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from accommodation — sandwiches, fruit, and trail mix eaten on the Kepler Track at Brod Bay (~NZD $4-5)
meals.dinner: Self-catered stir-fry with vegetables and noodles (~NZD $6-8 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Kepler Track to Brod Bay is an excellent, gentle introduction to Fiordland hiking. No permit needed for this day section. Wear layers — Fiordland weather can change rapidly even in November (spring/early summer).

day_by_day.morning: Full day on the Routeburn Track Day Hike. Depart Te Anau early (~7:00 AM) and drive to the Routeburn Shelter at the Glenorchy end (~1.5 hrs via Queenstown). Begin hiking the Routeburn Track toward the Routeburn Flats and Routeburn Falls Hut (~4 hrs return, ~8 km). Marvel at alpine meadows, waterfalls, and dramatic mountain scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hike or turn back from the Falls Hut depending on fitness level. Have lunch at the Routeburn Falls Hut area with panoramic views. Begin the return hike to the trailhead. This is one of New Zealand's Great Walks — absolutely breathtaking scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Te Anau (~1.5 hrs). Arrive by 6:00-7:00 PM. Rest tired legs and cook dinner at accommodation. Optional: visit Fiordland Cinema in Te Anau to watch the 'Ata Whenua - Shadowland' film about Fiordland (~NZD $15) for an inspiring evening.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before departure — muesli bars, banana, instant coffee (~NZD $3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Routeburn Falls Hut — wraps, cheese, apple, chocolate (~NZD $5-7)
meals.dinner: Self-catered baked potatoes with canned beans and cheese (~NZD $5-7 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Routeburn Track is one of the available experiences for this trip. Start early to avoid crowds and make the most of daylight. No day hike permit required for this section. Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and a rain jacket. Insect repellent recommended for sandflies.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the iconic Milford Sound Road from Te Anau (~2.5 hrs each way). Depart by 7:30 AM. Stop at Mirror Lakes (free boardwalk, 15 min) and the Avenue of the Disappearing Mountain for photos. Walk through the Homer Tunnel and descend into the fiord.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Milford Sound. Take a budget cruise on Milford Sound — Real Journeys or Cruise Milford offer nature cruises from ~NZD $45-65 per person. See Mitre Peak, Stirling Falls, and wildlife including fur seals and dolphins. Alternatively, walk the Milford Sound foreshore track (free) if budget is very tight.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Te Anau along the scenic Milford Road. Arrive by 7:00-8:00 PM. Cook a simple dinner and rest — today involves a lot of driving (~5 hrs total).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast at accommodation before departure (~NZD $3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Milford Sound foreshore — avoid the expensive Milford Sound Lodge cafe (~NZD $5-7)
meals.dinner: Self-catered soup and bread at accommodation (~NZD $4-6 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Milford Sound cruise in advance online for the best budget rates. The Milford Road is one of the most scenic drives in the world — allow extra time for stops. Sandflies are intense at Milford Sound — bring strong repellent. Check for road conditions and tunnel schedules before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning at Te Anau — sleep in and recover from the big days. Visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves for a guided boat tour (~NZD $55-75 per person, book in advance). The caves feature stunning glowworm grotto accessible only by boat — a truly unique Fiordland experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the short Luxmore Grunt trail section of the Kepler Track above the treeline for panoramic views of Lake Te Anau and the surrounding mountains (~3-4 hrs return from Control Gates carpark, free). This more challenging section offers incredible alpine scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a budget dinner out in Te Anau as a reward for the week's hiking. Explore Te Anau township's small selection of cafes and restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered cooked breakfast — eggs on toast at accommodation (~NZD $4-5)
meals.lunch: Self-catered packed lunch on the Kepler Track (~NZD $5)
meals.dinner: Budget dinner at The Sandfly Cafe or Miles Better Pies in Te Anau — fish and chips or a hearty pie (~NZD $15-20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Te Anau Glowworm Caves tour is run by Real Journeys and must be booked in advance. This is one of the top highlights of the Te Anau area. The Luxmore Grunt section of the Kepler is more strenuous — only attempt in good weather with proper footwear.

day_by_day.morning: Pack up and check out of Te Anau Boutique Stay. Drive north toward Queenstown (~2 hrs). Stop at the Devil's Staircase lookout on the Remarkables for views over Lake Wakatipu. Arrive in Queenstown by mid-morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Queenstown is the adventure capital of New Zealand and the bungee jumping hub. This afternoon, do the Kawarau Bridge Bungee Jump (~NZD $165-195 per person) — the world's first commercial bungee site, a 43m jump above the turquoise Kawarau River. Book in advance online for best rates. Alternatively, the Ledge Bungee in Queenstown (~NZD $165) offers a 47m urban jump with lake views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's buzzing lakefront and Steamer Wharf area. Watch the sunset over The Remarkables mountain range from the waterfront — free and spectacular. Find budget accommodation in Queenstown (hostel dorm ~NZD $35-50/night, e.g., Base Queenstown or Nomads Queenstown).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered final breakfast at Te Anau accommodation before checkout (~NZD $3)
meals.lunch: Fergburger in Queenstown — the legendary budget-friendly burger institution (~NZD $15-18). Arrive early to avoid queues.
meals.dinner: Self-catered meal using hostel kitchen, or grab cheap pizza from Queenstown's Vudu Cafe or takeaway options (~NZD $12-15)

day_by_day.notes: Budget accommodation shifts to a hostel in Queenstown for the remainder of the trip. Book the bungee jump well in advance — Kawarau Bridge is iconic and fills up. Queenstown has many free activities including lakefront walks, the Queenstown Gardens, and the Ben Lomond trail access.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the Ben Lomond Track from Queenstown township — one of the best free hikes in the area. The trail starts from the Queenstown Gardens and climbs steeply through forest to alpine terrain. Hike to the saddle (~3 hrs return to saddle) or summit (~5-6 hrs return, 1748m) for 360° views of Queenstown, Lake Wakatipu, and the Remarkables.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue summit push or descend and explore Queenstown Gardens (free). Visit the free Kiwi Birdlife Park viewing area outside the park fence, or pay entry (~NZD $49) to see kiwi birds if budget allows. Browse the Queenstown waterfront markets on weekends.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the hostel. Socialize with other travelers. Cook in the hostel kitchen or grab cheap takeaways from the Queenstown Night Market (Saturdays, ~NZD $10-15 for street food).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered hostel breakfast — instant oats and coffee (~NZD $2-3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on Ben Lomond Track — peanut butter sandwiches, trail mix, energy bars (~NZD $4-5)
meals.dinner: Queenstown Saturday Night Market street food — dumplings, noodles, or wraps (~NZD $10-15)

day_by_day.notes: Ben Lomond is a challenging hike — start early and check weather forecasts. The summit section is exposed and can be windy. Bring warm layers, water, and sunscreen. The hike is completely free and offers arguably the best views in the Queenstown area.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown to Wanaka (~1 hr via Crown Range Road — the highest sealed road in NZ with incredible views, or via Cardrona). Stop at the Crown Range Summit lookout for panoramic views. Arrive in Wanaka by mid-morning. Walk around the Wanaka lakefront and see the famous 'That Wanaka Tree' — a lone willow growing in the lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Roy's Peak Track from Wanaka (~5-6 hrs return, 16 km, 1578m summit). This iconic hike offers the most photographed view in New Zealand — a rocky ridge overlooking Lake Wanaka with snow-capped Mount Aspiring in the background. Start by 1:00 PM at the latest for a safe return before dark.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Wanaka township. Grab dinner and explore the small but vibrant town. Wanaka has a more relaxed vibe than Queenstown. Find budget accommodation at Wanaka Bakpaka or Purple Cow Hostel (~NZD $35-50/night).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered hostel breakfast in Queenstown before departure (~NZD $2-3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on Roy's Peak — essential as there are no facilities on the trail (~NZD $5-7)
meals.dinner: Kai Whakapai Cafe & Bar in Wanaka for budget-friendly meals, or grab fish and chips from Wanaka takeaways (~NZD $12-18)

day_by_day.notes: Roy's Peak is closed from October 1 to November 10 for lambing season — by November 22 it should be open, but confirm with DOC before hiking. The hike is steep and exposed. Start as early in the afternoon as possible. The Crown Range Road is scenic but winding — drive carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Mount Aspiring National Park day hikes from Wanaka. Drive to the Raspberry Creek carpark (~45 min from Wanaka) and hike the Aspiring Hut Track (~4 hrs return, 11 km) along the Matukituki River Valley with views of Mount Aspiring (Tititea). Beautiful river flats, swing bridges, and beech forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Aspiring Hut for lunch and views, then return via the same track. Alternatively, explore the Rob Roy Glacier Track (~4 hrs return, 10 km) from the same carpark — a spectacular hike to a hanging glacier with waterfalls. Both tracks are free DOC maintained trails.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Wanaka. Visit Puzzling World (~NZD $18) for a quirky, budget-friendly evening activity, or simply enjoy the lakefront sunset for free. Cook dinner at the hostel.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered hostel breakfast — muesli and yogurt (~NZD $3-4)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Aspiring Hut or Rob Roy Glacier viewpoint (~NZD $5-7)
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta with pesto at hostel kitchen (~NZD $5-7 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Rob Roy Glacier Track is highly recommended and one of the best day hikes in New Zealand. The Raspberry Creek carpark has limited spaces — arrive early. River crossings may be required in high water — check conditions with DOC Wanaka office. Bring sandfly repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Wanaka to Nelson/Abel Tasman region (~5-6 hrs via State Highway 6 through Haast Pass). This is one of the great scenic drives of the South Island — pass through the Haast Pass, stop at Thunder Creek Falls (5 min walk from roadside, free) and the Gates of Haast bridge. Drive along the wild West Coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving north along the West Coast. Stop at Hokitika (~1 hr north of Haast) — visit the Hokitika Gorge (~30 min detour, free) with its stunning turquoise water and swing bridge. Continue toward Nelson (~3 hrs from Hokitika). Arrive in Nelson by early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Check into budget accommodation in Nelson (hostel ~NZD $35-50/night, e.g., Nelson City YHA or Paradiso Backpackers). Explore Nelson's compact city center and grab dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast at Wanaka hostel before the long drive (~NZD $3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at a roadside stop along Haast Pass — Thunder Creek Falls or Lake Paringa (~NZD $5-7)
meals.dinner: Budget dinner in Nelson — Stefano's Pizzeria or a takeaway from Nelson's CBD (~NZD $12-18)

day_by_day.notes: Day 10 is a significant driving day (~5-6 hrs). Start early from Wanaka by 7:30-8:00 AM. The Haast Pass route (SH6) is stunning but remote — fill up on petrol in Wanaka and again in Hokitika. The Hokitika Gorge detour is absolutely worth it. Check road conditions before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Nelson to the Abel Tasman National Park trailhead at Marahau (~1 hr). Begin the Abel Tasman Coast Track Day Hike — one of New Zealand's Great Walks. Hike from Marahau to Anchorage Bay (~3-4 hrs, ~12 km one way) through lush coastal forest, golden beaches, and turquoise bays.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend time at Anchorage Bay — swim in the crystal-clear water, have lunch on the beach, and explore the beautiful coastline. Return hike to Marahau (~3-4 hrs) or take a water taxi back (~NZD $35-45, book in advance with Abel Tasman Aquataxi) to save legs for the next day.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Nelson (~1 hr). Rest and recover. Cook dinner at the hostel or explore Nelson's evening dining scene.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered hostel breakfast before departure (~NZD $3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten on Anchorage Beach — the perfect picnic setting (~NZD $6-8)
meals.dinner: Self-catered meal at hostel kitchen, or grab a cheap meal from Nelson's supermarket deli (~NZD $8-12)

day_by_day.notes: The Abel Tasman Coast Track is the second available experience for this trip. The full one-way hike to Anchorage is ~12 km each way — consider the water taxi return to save energy. The park is stunning in November with warm weather and longer daylight hours. Bring togs (swimwear) for beach swimming. No permit needed for day hiking.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Abel Tasman further — drive to Totaranui at the northern end of the park (~1.5 hrs from Nelson via Takaka Hill) and hike the Totaranui to Anapai Bay section (~2 hrs return) for a quieter, less-visited stretch of the coast with pristine beaches and native forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back over the Takaka Hill (Marble Mountain) and stop at the Ngarua Caves (~NZD $20 guided tour) — impressive limestone caves with stalactites and moa bones. Continue to Kaiteriteri Beach (~30 min from Marahau) — one of the most beautiful beaches in New Zealand with golden sand and clear water. Swim and relax.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Nelson (~1 hr). Final evening in Nelson — treat yourself to a meal out at a Nelson restaurant. Nelson is known for its craft beer scene — try a local brew at Free House or Sprig & Fern (~NZD $8-10 per pint).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered hostel breakfast (~NZD $3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Totaranui Beach or Kaiteriteri Beach (~NZD $5-7)
meals.dinner: Budget dinner out in Nelson — Sprig & Fern Tavern for pub meals and local craft beer (~NZD $18-25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Totaranui road is narrow and winding — drive carefully. The Takaka Hill road is also steep and winding. Kaiteriteri Beach is a must-visit — one of the most beautiful beaches in New Zealand. Nelson has excellent craft beer and local wine — worth exploring the local food scene on the final full evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Nelson. Visit the Nelson Saturday Farmers Market at Montgomery Square (if timing aligns — check if open on Fridays) or explore the Nelson Arts Quarter and Christ Church Cathedral grounds (free). Visit the Centre of New Zealand marker — a short 20-minute uphill walk from the city center with panoramic views of Nelson and Tasman Bay (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight, drive to Nelson Airport (~10 min from city center) or Blenheim/Marlborough Airport (~1.5 hrs) for onward travel. Return the rental car. Allow plenty of time for car return and check-in. Do a final supermarket stop for snacks and use up remaining NZD cash.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Nelson or fly to Christchurch/Auckland for international connections. Reflect on an incredible 13 days exploring the South Island's most spectacular landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered final hostel breakfast or grab a coffee and muffin from a Nelson cafe (~NZD $6-8)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Nelson airport cafe or packed food from supermarket (~NZD $8-12)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight meal depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return flight details and airport. Nelson Airport (NSN) has domestic connections to Auckland and Wellington. Allow extra time for rental car return. Keep NZD $50-100 as buffer for airport costs and final expenses. This concludes an epic 13-day South Island adventure covering Fiordland, Queenstown, Wanaka, and the Abel Tasman — all on a budget!

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Christchurch International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, clear customs, and pick up pre-booked rental car.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive from Christchurch toward the first stop or rest area. Spend the afternoon exploring Christchurch city centre — visit the Botanic Gardens and the Re:START container mall. Stretch your legs after the flight with a leisurely walk along the Avon River.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a mid-range hotel in Christchurch (e.g., Distinction Christchurch Hotel). Settle in and enjoy a relaxed first evening in New Zealand.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a coffee and snack at the airport on arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a casual bite at Christchurch Airport or a nearby café such as C1 Espresso in the city centre.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Pog Mahone's Irish Bar & Restaurant or Fiddlesticks — relaxed atmosphere, mid-range pricing, great local cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Focus on recovering from the flight, adjusting to the time zone, and getting oriented. Confirm rental car and check all gear for the days ahead. Drive on the left in New Zealand.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning drive south from Christchurch toward Lake Tekapo (approx. 3 hours). Stop at the Church of the Good Shepherd and walk the short trail around Lake Tekapo's stunning turquoise shores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving south toward Queenstown (approx. 3.5 hours from Tekapo). Stop at Lindis Pass for panoramic tussock-covered hill views. Arrive in Queenstown by late afternoon and check in to mid-range accommodation (e.g., Novotel Queenstown Lakeside).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Queenstown waterfront and explore the vibrant town centre. Browse the shops on Beach Street and enjoy the lakeside atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Christchurch hotel or a quick stop at a café before departure.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Lake Tekapo — pick up supplies from a local Four Square supermarket or grab a pie from a bakery en route.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Fergburger (iconic Queenstown experience, great value) or Rata Restaurant for a slightly elevated mid-range meal.

day_by_day.notes: Total driving today is approximately 6–7 hours with stops. Start early (7:00–8:00 AM) to arrive in Queenstown comfortably. Queenstown will serve as a base for the next two nights.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Kawarau Bridge (20 minutes from Queenstown) for the iconic Kawarau Bridge Bungee Jump — the world's first commercial bungee site, a thrilling 43-metre plunge above the stunning Kawarau River gorge. Book in advance to secure your time slot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown and take the Skyline Gondola up Bob's Peak for panoramic views of the Remarkables mountain range and Lake Wakatipu. Enjoy the luge or simply soak in the scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's buzzing nightlife strip. Enjoy dinner and unwind after the adrenaline-filled day.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a Queenstown café such as Vudu Café & Larder — excellent coffee and fresh baked goods.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Skyline Gondola complex restaurant with panoramic views, or grab a quick bite back in town at a food truck.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Winnies Queenstown (great pizza and atmosphere) or The Bunker for a cosy mid-range dinner experience.

day_by_day.notes: Kawarau Bungee must be booked in advance through AJ Hackett Bungy NZ. Arrive at the bridge 15 minutes before your slot. Wear comfortable clothing and closed-toe shoes. The jump is weather-dependent but rarely cancelled.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown to Glenorchy (45 minutes) for a scenic morning walk around the Glenorchy Lagoon Walkway and Paradise area — dramatic mountain and river scenery used in Lord of the Rings filming.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back through Queenstown and continue south toward Te Anau (approx. 2 hours). Check in to Te Anau Boutique Stay in Fiordland National Park — your home base for the next several nights. Spend the afternoon getting settled and taking a peaceful walk along the Te Anau lakefront.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the small but charming town of Te Anau. Visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves booking office to confirm any tours. Enjoy a quiet evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Queenstown accommodation or at a café before departing.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy in the Glenorchy/Paradise area — pick up supplies from a Queenstown supermarket the night before.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Moose (Te Anau) — a popular local restaurant with a great selection of New Zealand dishes at mid-range prices.

day_by_day.notes: Te Anau is the gateway to Fiordland National Park and your base for the next several days. Stock up on groceries and any hiking supplies in Te Anau town before heading to the boutique stay. Confirm Milford Track booking details.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the Milford Track Great Walk — Day 1. Take the ferry from Te Anau Downs to the track start at Glade Wharf (ferry departs approximately 10:00 AM, pre-booking essential). Hike 5 km through the beech forest to Clinton Hut. Enjoy the serene valley and river scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Clinton Hut (DOC Great Walk hut) by early afternoon. Explore the surrounding area, rest, and take short walks near the hut. Spot native birds including kea and robins.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Clinton Hut. Cook dinner using your packed supplies (hut has cooking facilities). Socialise with fellow trampers and enjoy the peaceful Fiordland evening.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Te Anau Boutique Stay before heading to Te Anau Downs.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail — sandwiches, trail mix, energy bars prepared the evening before.
meals.dinner: Self-cooked meal at Clinton Hut — lightweight dehydrated meals or pre-prepared food carried in.

day_by_day.notes: Milford Track Great Walk requires advance DOC booking (opens months in advance). Guided or independent options available — independent guided hut passes required. Pack all food for 4 days on the track. Carry rain gear — Fiordland receives very high rainfall. Day 1 is relatively easy (5 km).

day_by_day.morning: Milford Track Day 2. Depart Clinton Hut early and hike 16.5 km to Mintaro Hut. The trail follows the Clinton River through lush beech forest and open valley floors with towering granite walls on either side.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking through the stunning Clinton Valley. Pass through the alpine meadows and enjoy views of the surrounding peaks. Arrive at Mintaro Hut in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at Mintaro Hut. Tomorrow's MacKinnon Pass crossing is the highlight — check weather conditions with hut wardens. Prepare gear for an early start. Enjoy the mountain atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Self-cooked breakfast at Clinton Hut before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail.
meals.dinner: Self-cooked meal at Mintaro Hut.

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is a moderate 16.5 km hike. Pace yourself and enjoy the scenery. The Clinton Valley is one of the most beautiful sections of the track. Stay hydrated and watch for sandflies — bring insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Track Day 3 — the most dramatic day. Depart early to climb to MacKinnon Pass (1,154 m) — the highest point of the track with 360-degree alpine views. This is the iconic highlight of the entire walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend steeply from MacKinnon Pass through the Arthur Valley. Pass the spectacular Sutherland Falls (580 m — one of the world's tallest waterfalls) via a short side trip. Arrive at Dumpling Hut (21.5 km total for the day).
day_by_day.evening: Rest well at Dumpling Hut — today is the longest and most physically demanding day. Treat any blisters, stretch, and prepare for the final day tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Early self-cooked breakfast at Mintaro Hut — depart by 7:00 AM.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at MacKinnon Pass shelter.
meals.dinner: Self-cooked meal at Dumpling Hut — well-deserved after a big day.

day_by_day.notes: Day 3 is 21.5 km and the most challenging day. MacKinnon Pass can be subject to severe weather — hut wardens will advise if conditions are unsafe. The Sutherland Falls side trip adds approximately 1 hour but is absolutely worth it. Start early to allow plenty of time.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Track Day 4 — final day. Hike 18 km from Dumpling Hut to Sandfly Point through rainforest and along the Arthur River. The terrain is gentler today with beautiful river and forest scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Sandfly Point and take the ferry to Milford Sound. Enjoy your first views of the iconic Milford Sound fiord. Board a scenic Milford Sound cruise (1.5–2 hours) to celebrate completing the Great Walk.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Te Anau from Milford Sound (approx. 2 hours). Return to Te Anau Boutique Stay, shower, and celebrate completing one of the world's greatest walks.

meals.breakfast: Self-cooked breakfast at Dumpling Hut.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the final section of the trail.
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Redcliff Restaurant in Te Anau — excellent New Zealand cuisine in a mid-range setting, perfect for marking the achievement.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Milford Sound cruise in advance through Real Journeys or Go Orange. The drive back from Milford Sound to Te Anau takes approximately 2 hours on a scenic road — take your time and enjoy it. You have earned a great rest tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Well-deserved rest morning at Te Anau Boutique Stay. Sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and recover from the Milford Track. Do laundry and repack gear.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves (book in advance through Real Journeys) — a magical underground boat tour through glowworm-lit caves beneath Lake Te Anau. Tour duration approximately 2.5 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Te Anau. Browse the lakefront and enjoy the sunset over Lake Te Anau.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at Te Anau Boutique Stay or at a local café such as Miles Better Pies.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Te Anau café — try The Fat Duck or grab a pie from a local bakery.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sandfly Café or Ristorante Pizzeria Leonardo's — relaxed mid-range dining in Te Anau.

day_by_day.notes: This is a planned recovery day after four days on the Milford Track. Listen to your body and rest as needed. The glowworm caves tour is a gentle, low-impact activity perfect for a recovery day. Book the caves tour well in advance as it is popular.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Te Anau to the Routeburn Track trailhead at The Divide (approx. 1.5 hours via the Milford Road). Begin the Routeburn Track Day Hike — hike from The Divide up to Key Summit (2.5 hours return) for panoramic views of the Hollyford, Greenstone, and Eglinton Valleys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking along the Routeburn Track toward Lake Howden Hut and beyond if energy allows. Enjoy the subalpine tussock landscape and crystal-clear mountain tarns. Return to The Divide trailhead.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Te Anau (1.5 hours). Relax at the boutique stay and enjoy a quiet evening.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Te Anau Boutique Stay before the drive.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail at Key Summit — enjoy the views while you eat.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Moose in Te Anau — hearty New Zealand fare to refuel after hiking.

day_by_day.notes: The Key Summit loop from The Divide is one of the best day hikes in Fiordland — highly recommended. No hut booking required for a day hike. Wear layers as the summit can be cool and windy even in November. The Milford Road itself is scenic — allow extra time for stops.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Te Anau and drive north toward Hanmer Springs (approx. 6–7 hours via Queenstown and the inland scenic route). Stop in Queenstown for a short break and coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving north through the Canterbury high country. Arrive at Hanmer Springs in the late afternoon. Check in to mid-range accommodation (e.g., Hanmer Springs Hotel or Scenic Hotel Thermal Pools & Spa).
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the Hanmer Springs Thermal Pools & Spa — the perfect way to relax tired muscles after days of hiking. Enjoy the outdoor thermal pools under the evening sky.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Te Anau Boutique Stay before checking out.
meals.lunch: Stop for lunch in Queenstown or at a roadside café en route — try a local bakery or pub.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Coriander's Restaurant in Hanmer Springs — popular local restaurant with a good mid-range menu.

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — start early (7:00–8:00 AM). The drive through the Southern Alps and Canterbury high country is stunning. Hanmer Springs is a charming alpine village — a great contrast to the Fiordland wilderness. Confirm Hanmer Springs Bungy booking for tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Experience the Hanmer Springs Bungy & Swing — a 35-metre jump over a scenic river gorge combined with the thrilling Catapult Swing. Book the first morning slot for maximum energy and excitement.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Hanmer Springs village on foot. Visit the Hanmer Springs Forest Park for a gentle walk along the Woodland Walk or Dog Stream Waterfall Track — a beautiful contrast to the morning's adrenaline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the thermal pools for a final soak. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and reflect on the incredible 12 days of adventure.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Hanmer Springs accommodation or a local café before the bungy.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Hanmer Springs café — try Powerhouse Café for great food in a relaxed setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malabar Restaurant in Hanmer Springs — excellent Asian-fusion cuisine at mid-range prices, a local favourite.

day_by_day.notes: Hanmer Springs Bungy is operated by Hanmer Springs Attractions — book directly on their website. The Bungy & Swing combo is excellent value. Minimum weight requirements apply. This is your second bungee experience of the trip — a great bookend to the Kawarau jump on Day 3.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Hanmer Springs and drive back to Christchurch (approx. 1.5 hours). Stop at Waipara Valley on the way for a visit to a local winery — the region is known for excellent Pinot Noir and Riesling. Enjoy a morning tasting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Christchurch. Spend the final afternoon exploring anything missed on Day 1 — visit the Canterbury Museum (free entry), the Christchurch Art Gallery, or explore the vibrant Addington or Sydenham neighbourhoods.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Christchurch to celebrate an incredible 13-day South Island adventure. Head to the airport for departure or check in to an airport hotel if flying the next morning.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Hanmer Springs accommodation before checking out.
meals.lunch: Winery lunch at Waipara Valley — many wineries such as Pegasus Bay offer excellent restaurant lunches with local produce.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Gatherings Restaurant or Hello Sunday in Christchurch — excellent modern New Zealand cuisine at mid-range prices.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight time and allow sufficient time to reach Christchurch Airport. Return the rental car with a full tank of petrol — rental companies charge premium rates for fuel if not returned full. Keep receipts for any travel insurance claims. This final day provides a wonderful, relaxed close to an action-packed South Island adventure.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Fiordland National Park, Te Anau Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Milford Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of the world's greatest walks through Fiordland National Park, passing stunning valleys, waterfalls, and alpine scenery over 4 days. Book huts in advance through DOC. The trail winds from Lake Te Anau to Milford Sound through pristine wilderness.

experiences.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungee Jump
experiences.description: Take the plunge at the world's first commercial bungee jumping site, a 43-metre jump above the stunning turquoise Kawarau River. Watch others jump from the viewing platform before taking your own leap. An iconic adrenaline experience that started it all in 1988.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Day Hike
experiences.description: Explore a section of the famous Routeburn Track, one of New Zealand's Great Walks, offering breathtaking alpine views, glacier-carved valleys, and diverse native birdlife. The track traverses the boundary of two national parks and rewards hikers with panoramic mountain vistas.

experiences.name: Hanmer Springs Bungy & Swing
experiences.description: Experience the Hanmer Springs Bungy, a 35-metre jump over a scenic river gorge, combined with the thrilling Ledge Swing for a double adrenaline hit. Set in the picturesque alpine village of Hanmer Springs, this is a more intimate and scenic bungee experience away from the Queenstown crowds.
experiences.location: Hanmer Springs Adventure Centre, Hanmer Springs

experiences.name: Abel Tasman Coast Track Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Abel Tasman National Park along golden sandy beaches, turquoise bays, and lush native forest. This accessible coastal walk offers a unique combination of beach and bush hiking, with opportunities to spot fur seals and native birds. Water taxis can be used to customize your route.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Queenstown Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage and meet your private transfer driver.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Queenstown Airport to Te Anau Boutique Stay in Fiordland National Park (~2.5 hours). Enjoy the scenic drive through Central Otago and the Wakatipu Basin. Check in, settle into your boutique accommodation, and take a leisurely stroll around the shores of Lake Te Anau to decompress from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at the Te Anau boutique lodge's private dining experience or at the renowned Redcliff Restaurant in Te Anau township, known for its South Island game meats, fresh local salmon, and fine Central Otago wines. Relax and acclimatise.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport lounge meal
meals.lunch: Light refreshments provided during private transfer, or a stop at a scenic café en route (e.g., Queenstown's Vudu Café for a premium grazing board)
meals.dinner: Redcliff Restaurant, Te Anau — three-course dinner featuring venison, blue cod, and local Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep the schedule relaxed. Confirm all activity bookings for the coming days with your concierge. Hydrate well and get an early night to prepare for the Milford Track experience ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided walk along the Te Anau lakefront and through the native beech forest reserve. Birdwatch for kea, tūī, and bellbirds with a private naturalist guide. Enjoy the crisp Fiordland air and stunning views of the Murchison Mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Te Anau Glowworm Caves exclusive private tour — cruise across Lake Te Anau and explore the magical underground limestone cave system illuminated by thousands of glowworms. This premium private tour avoids the crowds and includes a personal guide explaining the geology and Māori legends.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the lodge terrace overlooking Lake Te Anau, followed by a private chef's tasting menu at the boutique stay featuring Fiordland crayfish, South Island lamb, and artisan New Zealand cheeses.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the boutique lodge — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh fruit, artisan breads, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic hamper prepared by the lodge, enjoyed lakeside after the glowworm cave tour
meals.dinner: Private chef's tasting menu at Te Anau Boutique Stay — six courses with matched Central Otago wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book the private glowworm cave tour well in advance as exclusive slots are limited. Wear comfortable walking shoes and a light waterproof jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the Milford Track Great Walk — Day 1 on trail. Depart Te Anau by private boat across Lake Te Anau to the Glade Wharf trailhead. Hike through the serene Glade Burn valley, surrounded by ancient beech forest. This first section (~5 km) is relatively flat and sets the tone for the epic journey ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the Clinton River valley, passing through pristine wilderness with towering peaks on either side. Arrive at the luxurious private lodge (Ultimate Hikes' Glade House equivalent — premium guided walk accommodation) by mid-afternoon. Freshen up and enjoy the surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Guided evening talk by a Fiordland naturalist about the ecology, history, and wildlife of the Milford Track. Three-course communal dinner at the lodge with fellow premium walkers, featuring hearty South Island cuisine and fine wines.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet lodge breakfast — hot porridge, eggs to order, fresh juices, and coffee before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch prepared by the lodge, enjoyed trailside beside the Clinton River
meals.dinner: Three-course dinner at the private guided walk lodge — roasted lamb, seasonal vegetables, and New Zealand dessert wines

day_by_day.notes: This is Day 1 of the multi-day Milford Track experience on the premium guided walk. All gear, meals, and transfers are handled by the guided walk operator. Pack only a day pack — porters carry main luggage between lodges.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Track Day 2 — Hike from Glade House to Pompolona Lodge (~16.5 km). Cross the swing bridge over the Clinton River and ascend gradually through open valley floors with dramatic views of Mt. Balloon and the surrounding peaks. Pass through meadows filled with alpine wildflowers blooming in the November spring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the ascent towards Mintaro Hut area, with optional side trip to the base of the Hidden Lake for a stunning reflection of the Fiordland peaks. Arrive at Pompolona Lodge in the afternoon. Soak tired legs in the lodge's foot spa and enjoy panoramic mountain views from the deck.
day_by_day.evening: Guided stargazing session in Fiordland's exceptionally dark skies — one of the best stargazing locations in the Southern Hemisphere. Dinner at the lodge featuring slow-cooked venison stew, freshly baked bread, and a selection of South Island red wines.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at Glade House before departing — scrambled eggs, bacon, toast, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch pack enjoyed at a scenic rest point along the Clinton Valley
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner at Pompolona — hearty three-course meal with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Today's hike is the longest day on the track. Pace yourself in the morning. November weather in Fiordland can be changeable — always carry full waterproofs and an extra layer regardless of morning conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Track Day 3 — The most spectacular day. Ascend to Mackinnon Pass (1,154 m), the high point of the track, with breathtaking 360-degree views over Fiordland. This is the crown jewel of the walk. Optional side trip to the Sutherland Falls — one of the world's tallest waterfalls at 580 m — a 30-minute return detour well worth every step.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend the dramatic zigzag trail down the Arthur Valley with stunning valley and waterfall views at every turn. Pass the Roaring Burn and walk through ancient rainforest to Quintin Lodge. Enjoy a well-earned hot shower and a massage treatment available at the premium lodge facility.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner at Quintin Lodge marking the completion of the hardest day on the track. Premium wine selection, a special dessert course, and a guided presentation on the history of the Milford Track's discovery and construction.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty hot breakfast at Pompolona Lodge to fuel the big ascent
meals.lunch: Summit picnic lunch at Mackinnon Pass — gourmet hamper with local cheeses, charcuterie, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Celebratory three-course dinner at Quintin Lodge with premium Central Otago Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: Mackinnon Pass can be cold and windy even in November — full waterproofs, gloves, and a warm mid-layer are essential. The Sutherland Falls side trip adds approximately 1 hour — highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Track Day 4 — Final stage. Hike from Quintin Lodge to Sandfly Point (~18 km), the trail's end at Milford Sound. Walk through lush rainforest draped in mosses and ferns, cross numerous swing bridges, and enjoy the final approach through the dramatic Milford valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Sandfly Point and take the ferry across to Milford Sound. Board a private luxury Milford Sound cruise — glide past the iconic Mitre Peak, beneath towering waterfalls including Lady Bowen Falls, and spot fur seals, dolphins, and penguins in their natural habitat. Celebrate completing the Milford Track with champagne on deck.
day_by_day.evening: Private helicopter flight back from Milford Sound to Te Anau for a spectacular aerial perspective of Fiordland — mountains, fiords, and untouched wilderness from above. Return to Te Anau Boutique Stay. Relaxing dinner at the lodge celebrating the completion of the Milford Track.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast at Quintin — fuel up for the last day on the trail
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch pack enjoyed trailside on the final section, or light refreshments on the Milford Sound cruise
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at Te Anau Boutique Stay — premium seafood platter with Fiordland crayfish, oysters, and chilled Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: The helicopter transfer from Milford Sound to Te Anau (~25 minutes) is a spectacular way to end the Milford Track experience. Book well in advance. Sandfly repellent is essential at Sandfly Point.

day_by_day.morning: Well-deserved rest morning at Te Anau Boutique Stay. Enjoy a late, leisurely gourmet breakfast, an in-lodge spa treatment (massage or body wrap to recover muscles after four days on the Milford Track), and gentle yoga or stretching session arranged by the lodge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic drive from Te Anau to Queenstown (~2.5 hours) via the Kingston Flyer route and along the shores of Lake Wakatipu. Stop at the Kawarau Gorge scenic lookout. Check in to a luxury Queenstown hotel (e.g., Eichardt's Private Hotel or The Rees Hotel on the lakefront).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's vibrant waterfront precinct. Pre-dinner cocktails at Eichardt's Bar — one of New Zealand's most celebrated cocktail bars with stunning lake views. Dinner at Amisfield Bistro or Rata restaurant, both icons of Queenstown fine dining.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent late breakfast at Te Anau Boutique Stay — full cooked spread with pastries, smoked fish, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Scenic lunch stop en route to Queenstown at a lakeside café (e.g., Queenstown Hill Café or Sherwood dining room)
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant, Queenstown — Chef Josh Emmett's celebrated New Zealand cuisine with premium wine list

day_by_day.notes: Recovery day is important after the Milford Track. Prioritise the spa treatment and don't over-schedule. Queenstown hotel check-in is typically from 3:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Kawarau Bridge Bungee Jump — Take the iconic 43-metre plunge at the world's first commercial bungee jumping site above the stunning turquoise Kawarau River. This is a bucket-list experience. Opt for the tandem jump or solo. The Kawarau Bridge site also has a viewing platform and AJ Hackett's premium VIP experience with champagne post-jump.
day_by_day.afternoon: Routeburn Track Day Hike — Drive to the Routeburn trailhead (approximately 1 hour from Queenstown) and hike a premium guided section of the famous Routeburn Track. Explore the lower valley section through ancient beech forest with views of the Humboldt Mountains. A private guide will provide ecological and cultural context throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown. Sunset gondola ride up Bob's Peak for panoramic views over Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables mountain range. Dinner at Kō Restaurant at the Hilton or The Bunker — Queenstown's most intimate fine dining venue.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet hotel breakfast at Queenstown luxury accommodation
meals.lunch: Trailside picnic lunch on the Routeburn Track — premium hamper prepared by the hotel with artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, and fruit
meals.dinner: The Bunker Restaurant, Queenstown — intimate fine dining with outstanding New Zealand beef, game, and wine selection

day_by_day.notes: The Kawarau Bridge bungee and Routeburn hike can be combined in one day but ensure the bungee is booked for early morning (9:00–10:00 AM) to allow enough time for the afternoon hike. Confirm Routeburn guide booking in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private heli-hiking experience — Fly by helicopter to a remote alpine zone above Queenstown (e.g., the Richardson Mountains or Cecil Peak) and hike with a private mountain guide through untouched high-alpine terrain with extraordinary views. This exclusive experience combines the thrill of helicopter access with world-class hiking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown by helicopter. Afternoon at leisure — explore Queenstown's boutique shopping precinct, visit the Queenstown Gardens, or enjoy a private wine tasting experience at a lakefront venue showcasing Central Otago Pinot Noir from premium producers such as Amisfield, Peregrine, and Felton Road.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury sunset cruise on Lake Wakatipu aboard a private charter vessel — champagne, canapés, and uninterrupted views of the Remarkables, Cecil Peak, and Walter Peak as the sun sets. Dinner at Amisfield Winery (if not visited for dinner on Day 7) — farm-to-table cuisine in a stunning vineyard setting.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before the early helicopter departure
meals.lunch: Heli-picnic in the alpine zone — gourmet hamper delivered by the helicopter operator to your mountain location
meals.dinner: Amisfield Winery Bistro — trust the chef menu with matched Amisfield wines in a vineyard setting

day_by_day.notes: Heli-hiking is weather-dependent — have a backup activity arranged (e.g., Queenstown gondola and Luge, or a second wine tasting tour). Book the private lake cruise well in advance for sunset timing.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or private transfer from Queenstown to Hanmer Springs (~4 hours via the scenic Lewis Pass route through the Southern Alps). Stop at Lake Tekapo en route — visit the Church of the Good Shepherd, stroll the lakefront, and admire the impossibly turquoise glacial waters framed by lupins in bloom (November is peak lupin season).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Hanmer Springs. Check in to The Cheltenham House or Hanmer Springs premium accommodation. Hanmer Springs Bungy & Swing — experience the 35-metre Hanmer Springs Bungy jump above a scenic river gorge, followed by the thrilling Swing. A fantastic adrenaline combination in a beautiful natural setting.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the Hanmer Springs Thermal Pools private pools (exclusive evening session) to relax muscles after the day's adventures. Dinner at Monteith's Brewery Bar or the Heritage Hotel's restaurant — local craft beers, South Island lamb, and relaxed alpine dining.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Queenstown before departure
meals.lunch: Lake Tekapo lunch stop at Mackenzie's Bar & Grill or a lakeside café — fresh fish and chips or a gourmet burger with lake views
meals.dinner: Heritage Hotel Restaurant, Hanmer Springs — local game meats, seasonal vegetables, and South Island wines

day_by_day.notes: The drive via Lake Tekapo adds scenic value and is highly recommended in November when the lupins are in full bloom. Book the Hanmer Springs Bungy in advance. The private thermal pools session should be reserved for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Morning walk through the Hanmer Forest Park — a network of pine and native forest trails with mountain views. Optional horse trekking through the Hanmer Basin with a premium operator for a different perspective of the landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive from Hanmer Springs to Nelson/Abel Tasman region (~3 hours via the coastal Kaikōura route). Stop at Kaikōura for a scenic coastal walk along the Peninsula Walkway with excellent chances of seeing fur seals resting on the rocks. Check in to a premium Nelson or Mārahau accommodation (e.g., Awaroa Lodge in Abel Tasman National Park, accessible by water taxi).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset water taxi ride to Awaroa Lodge — a remote, eco-luxury lodge accessible only by boat, foot, or air, set within Abel Tasman National Park. Welcome drinks on the lodge deck overlooking Awaroa Inlet. Private dinner at the lodge featuring fresh seafood, local produce, and Marlborough wines.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Hanmer Springs accommodation
meals.lunch: Kaikōura seafood lunch — fresh crayfish, green-lipped mussels, and chowder at The Crayfish Pot or Nin's Bin roadside crayfish stall
meals.dinner: Awaroa Lodge Restaurant — remote fine dining with fresh Abel Tasman seafood and Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: Awaroa Lodge is one of New Zealand's most exclusive and remote luxury lodges — book well in advance. The water taxi from Mārahau to Awaroa takes approximately 1.5 hours and is an experience in itself.

day_by_day.morning: Abel Tasman Coast Track Hike — Guided hike along the golden sandy beaches and turquoise bays of Abel Tasman National Park from Awaroa. Walk through native coastal forest, cross tidal inlets, and swim in crystal-clear bays. November offers long daylight hours, warm temperatures, and relatively uncrowded trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the hike to Bark Bay or Torrent Bay, stopping to kayak in the sheltered bays (premium guided sea kayaking add-on available). Spot New Zealand fur seals, little blue penguins, and variable oystercatchers along the coastline. Water taxi return to Mārahau in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer back to Nelson city. Check in to a premium Nelson hotel (e.g., Trailways Hotel). Dinner at The Boat Shed Café on Nelson's waterfront — renowned for its fresh local seafood, particularly Nelson scallops, blue cod, and Marlborough oysters, with views over the marina.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Awaroa Lodge before hitting the trail
meals.lunch: Beach picnic lunch on a secluded Abel Tasman beach — gourmet hamper from the lodge with local cheeses, charcuterie, fresh fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: The Boat Shed Café, Nelson — fresh local seafood with Marlborough wine pairing in a stunning waterfront setting

day_by_day.notes: The Abel Tasman hike combined with kayaking is a full and rewarding day. Wear sunscreen and a hat — November sun in the Abel Tasman can be intense. Water taxis run to a tidal schedule so confirm timing with the operator the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Nelson — visit the Nelson Saturday Market (one of New Zealand's best artisan markets) for local crafts, food, and produce. Explore Nelson's vibrant arts precinct and visit the World of Wearable Art & Classic Cars Museum — a uniquely New Zealand cultural experience. Walk up to the geographical Centre of New Zealand lookout for panoramic views over Tasman Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell lunch in Nelson, then private transfer to Nelson Airport for onward flights. Alternatively, if the itinerary allows for a later departure, take a scenic flight over the Abel Tasman National Park and Golden Bay — a spectacular aerial farewell to the South Island.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Nelson Airport. Reflect on an extraordinary 13-day South Island journey encompassing the world's greatest walks, iconic bungee jumps, remote wilderness lodges, and world-class New Zealand cuisine and wine.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely gourmet hotel breakfast at Nelson accommodation — eggs, fresh pastries, local honey, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Hopgood's & Co, Nelson — one of the South Island's finest restaurants, celebrating the end of an extraordinary trip with premium New Zealand cuisine and wine
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge meal depending on departure schedule

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before departure for airport check-in, especially if connecting through Christchurch or Wellington to international flights. The scenic flight over Abel Tasman on departure day is weather-dependent — confirm availability with the operator. Consider purchasing premium New Zealand wines, Manuka honey, and artisan goods at the Nelson Market as souvenirs.

query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026
